subject: Short evaluation: proportional credits vs time-extension — ACME ML

Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Short evaluation: request for runway top-up or proportional credits

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the product demo yesterday — the team is excited. We have one operational ask from infra and procurement: our mini pilot (30-day timebox) is burning faster than expected due to heavy tokenizer experiments. Two options the stakeholders are willing to consider:

1) Add 10 calendar days to the current timebox (so total 40 days) with a 10% uplift on the monthly pilot fee.
2) Keep the 30-day box but receive proportional usage credits (tokens) that we can draw down over the next 45 days, effectively smoothing burst usage.

Procurement also asked whether any SLA carveouts or reduced latency targets are tied to an extension. They want something in writing before pushing to legal.

Can you share a quick pricing table for both options and confirm whether Redwood can provide a temporary SLA exception for the extra days? If neither is feasible, they asked for an equivalent credits-only path that is refundable/non-refundable (they prefer non-refundable credits).

Appreciate a short note and any required amendment draft.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Head of ML Platforms
ACME ML

Subject: Re: Short evaluation: request for runway top-up or proportional credits

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the metrics snapshot. Short answer: we can support both approaches; below is a concise comparison plus next steps. I attached a draft amendment and a one-page pricing matrix.

Option A — +10 days (40-day timebox):
- Price: 10% uplift on the agreed pilot rate for the additional period.
- Billing: one-time invoice upon amendment signature.
- SLA: we can agree a temporary carveout that maintains platform availability SLA but pauses latency SLO guarantees tied to capacity (so we won’t apply SLA credits for latency misses during the extra window). We will include explicit language in the amendment.

Option B — Proportional credits (tokens for smoothing):
- Price: Credits equivalent to the uplifted token usage at the pilot rate (non-refundable by default, but we can offer refundable credits under finance-approved exceptions).
- Drawdown window: credits usable over 45 days from issuance.
- Billing: invoice for credits up-front.

Operational notes:
- Either option does not change data residency or model versions in the pilot.
- If you want both an extension and credits (hybrid), we can provide a small bundled discount — happy to include numbers if you want that path.

Next steps (recommended):
1) Confirm preferred option by EOD Wed (3/17).
2) If Option A, sign amendment (attached) and we’ll schedule the invoice.
3) If Option B, we’ll issue a quote for the credits and set the drawdown window in the amendment.

Looping in Ben (sales ops) and Priyom (solutions) to help finalize pricing and the amendment language.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Quick internal note / price sanity check before we finalize:

- Base pilot rate = $12,000 (30-day timebox).
- Option A math: 10% uplift = $1,200 (one-time).
- Option B math: estimated token overage credit = $1,050 (we recommend rounding to $1,100 and offering 30-day drawdown as default; Elena requested 45d).

Recommendation: offer Option A at $1,200 (clean, easy for procurement) or Option B at $1,100 refundable on a case-by-case basis. Also propose a hybrid: +5 days + $600 credits at $950 bundled price as a good-faith concession (can be approved by Sales Ops).

Priyom: can you confirm if the SLA language in the attached amendment is acceptable operationally? If so, I’ll approve the concession and we can send to Elena.

-Ben

Thanks — reviewed the amendment and pricing matrix. Operational accept:

- SLA carveout language is okay: we will maintain uptime SLA and temporarily set latency SLOs to best-effort for the extension window; we will not apply SLA credits for latency during the carved-out days. That is consistent with prior short-run pilots.
- Drawdown window for credits at 45 days is acceptable. Finance prefers non-refundable credits but will approve refundable credits up to $1,000 on a case-by-case basis.
- The hybrid bundle (5 days + $600 credits at $950) is fine to offer as an escalation-free agreement for ACME.

Vanessa — you can send the amendment and the bundled pricing to Elena with the note that finance will only flag anything if they select refundable credits > $1,000.

Priyom Das
